note: Ps71 prayer of old age (corrected). Human IB (21 chars): TAKE-REFUGE + lifelong TRUST/HOPE (from youth, LEANED from before birth); continual PRAISE x5; enemies WATCH for his life + SEEK/SOUGHT his hurt; the great theme - TELL/REMIND/PROCLAIM x4 God's righteous deeds to another generation, with JOY + song into old age. God-qualifiers ~33 (righteousness x5, refuge/rescue/deliver/save, salvation, faithfulness, Holy-One, taught/wondrous-deeds/might/power, not-forsake, revive/comfort/redeem). Rock/fortress images + old-age/gray-hair markers + imprecation (shame/scorn/disgrace) = standalone. Every candidate roled.

dims.v: take refuge (chasah - in you, O LORD, do I take refuge)
pleading never to be put to shame
grounded in God his rock and refuge (v3)
resting on God's righteousness to deliver and save (v2)

'In you, O LORD, do I TAKE REFUGE (chasah); let me never be put to shame!' — the lifelong sheltering in God that opens the old man's prayer; chasah here the refuge-taking that has been the psalmist's whole life, resting on God's righteousness (the qualifier) to deliver and save
wicked (rasha - from the hand of the wicked)
the same foes who watch for his life (v10)

'Rescue me, O my God, from the hand of the WICKED (rasha), from the grasp of the unjust and cruel man' — the enemies the aged psalmist fears; rasha here the wicked whose grasp he begs God to rescue him from - the same foes who watch for his life (v10)
hope (tiqvah - you, O Lord GOD, are my hope)

'For you, O Lord GOD, are my HOPE (tiqvah), my trust from my youth' — hope in God spanning a whole life; tiqvah here God himself as the psalmist's hope since youth - a confidence not newly found in old age but lifelong, which he begs God not to disappoint (v9)
trust / confidence (mibtach - my trust from my youth)

'my TRUST (mibtach) from my youth' — confidence in God held since earliest days; mibtach here the trust that has been the ground of the psalmist's whole life, from youth to gray hairs - the settled reliance he now leans on in his weakness
lean / be sustained (samak - upon you I have leaned from before my birth)
from before birth, from the womb

'Upon you I have LEANED (samak) from before my birth; you are he who took me from my mother's womb' — dependence on God reaching back before memory; samak here the leaning of a lifetime, from the womb (the qualifier took) onward - a trust older than the psalmist's own awareness, ground of his continual praise
praise (tehillah - my praise is continually of you)
the praise that fills his mouth all day (v8)

'My PRAISE (tehillah) is continually of you' — worship as the constant occupation of a life leaned on God; tehillah here the ceaseless praise of the one sustained from the womb - his mouth filled with God's praise all the day (v8)
praise (tehillah - my mouth is filled with your praise)

'My mouth is filled with your PRAISE (tehillah), and with your glory all the day' — praise so constant it brims the mouth; tehillah here the all-day worship of the God whose glory (the qualifier) fills the psalmist's speech
watch / lie in wait (shamar - those who watch for my life)
the foes who seek his hurt (v13,24)

'those who WATCH (shamar) for my life consult together' — the enemies lying in wait, presuming God has forsaken him; shamar here the foes stalking the aged psalmist's life, taking his weakness as proof of abandonment (v11) - malice preying on the old
the same seeking his hurt at the psalm's close (v24)

'may those who SEEK (baqash) my hurt be covered with scorn' — the enemies bent on the psalmist's harm; baqash here the foes seeking his ruin, whom he prays God will put to shame - answered at the close (v24) when they are disappointed
hope / wait (yachal - I will hope continually)
confident God will revive and comfort him again (v20-21)

'But I will HOPE (yachal) continually and will praise you yet more and more' — hope renewed against the enemies' scorn; yachal here the steady waiting on God that only grows, confident he will revive and comfort again (v20-21) - hope that answers despair with more praise
praise (tehillah - praise you yet more and more)
'and will PRAISE (tehillah) you yet more and more' — worship that increases with the years; tehillah here praise that does not fade in old age but multiplies - the aging saint praising ever more
tell / recount (saphar - my mouth will tell of your righteous acts)
all the day, beyond his knowledge to number
the testimony renewed as reminding and proclaiming (v16-18)

'My mouth will TELL (saphar) of your righteous acts, of your deeds of salvation all the day' — the tireless recounting of God's saving righteousness; saphar here the testimony that fills the psalmist's speech - deeds so many he cannot number them, yet tells them still
remind / make mention (zakar - I will remind them of your righteousness)
coming with the mighty deeds of the Lord GOD
paired with telling and proclaiming God's deeds

'I will come with the mighty deeds of the Lord GOD; I will REMIND (zakar) them of your righteousness, yours alone' — testimony that God's righteousness stands alone; zakar here the making-mention of God's righteousness only - the aged witness insisting all saving deeds are God's, not his own
proclaim / declare (nagad - I still proclaim your wondrous deeds)
continued in proclaiming to the next generation (v18)

'O God, from my youth you have taught me, and I still PROCLAIM (nagad) your wondrous deeds' — lifelong learning issuing in lifelong witness; nagad here the declaring of God's wonders that began in youth (the qualifier taught) and has not ceased - a whole life of testimony, still going
proclaim / declare (nagad - until I proclaim your might to another generation)
God's might and power, to another generation
even to old age and gray hairs
the mission that keeps him from being forsaken

'even to old age and gray hairs, O God, do not forsake me, until I PROCLAIM (nagad) your might to another generation' — the one thing the old man still lives for; nagad here the passing-on of God's power to those to come - the reason he begs not to be forsaken, that the testimony reach the next generation
praise / give thanks (yadah - I will praise you with the harp)
paired with singing praises with the lyre

'I will also PRAISE (yadah) you with the harp for your faithfulness, O my God' — praise for God's proven reliability; yadah here the thankful worship of the delivered, offered on the harp for the faithfulness (the qualifier) that never failed him
sing praises (zamar - I will sing praises to you with the lyre)
paired with praise on the harp

'I will SING PRAISES (zamar) to you with the lyre, O Holy One of Israel' — music offered to the Holy One; zamar here the sung worship addressed to God the Holy One (the qualifier) - the aged psalmist's instruments still tuned to praise
shout for joy (ranan - my lips will shout for joy)
his soul which God has redeemed (v23)

'My lips will shout for JOY (ranan), when I sing praises to you; my soul also, which you have redeemed' — jubilation of the redeemed soul; ranan here the shout of joy that answers redemption (the qualifier) - the whole self, lips and soul, ringing with gladness
sing praises (zamar - when I sing praises to you)
paired with the shout of joy
'when I SING PRAISES (zamar) to you' — the singing that accompanies the joyful shout; zamar here the song of the redeemed soul, worship overflowing in music
talk / muse (hagah - my tongue will talk of your righteous help)
the lifelong testimony, now that the foes are shamed

'And my tongue will TALK (hagah) of your righteous help all the day long' — testimony as the constant murmur of the tongue; hagah here the all-day musing on God's righteous salvation (cf Ps1:2) - the psalm closing as it ran, in ceaseless witness to God's righteousness
seek (baqash - those who sought my hurt)
the seeking-hurt of v13, now brought to shame

'for they have been put to shame and disappointed who SOUGHT (baqash) my hurt' — the enemies' malice foiled; baqash here the foes who sought the psalmist's harm (v13), now themselves shamed - the prayer answered, malice turned back

v11: 'PURSUE (radaph) and seize him' - the enemies' plan to hunt the psalmist down, thinking God has abandoned him. Standalone (the enemies' act).
seize / lay hold (taphas - and seize him)
